items.title: Is Tesla Stock Priced For Its Earnings Or Its Robots?
items.summary: Tesla (TSLA) stock trades at about $364, roughly 169 times its adjusted earnings over the past twelve months, meaning normalized net income with stock-based compensation added back. On analysts' own 2027 estimates, the multiple is still steep. So the price leans on wider margins and on products still early in their ramps.

items.title: Prediction: Tesla’s Biggest Catalyst May Still Be Ahead
items.summary: Tesla's operating margins just collapsed to 1.4% and free cash flow turned negative, yet one forward catalyst is quietly building that could dwarf everything the company has delivered so far.

items.title: Can Rivian Automotive Stock Rally If Its Factory Catches Up With Demand?
items.summary: Rivian Automotive (RIVN) began delivering its mass-market R2 to outside customers in June, and the harder part now is building enough of them. Management still expects the car business to exit 2026 with a positive gross profit, which depends on how fast its plant in Normal, Illinois, ramps.

items.title: Should You Buy Ford Motor Stock Because It Is Selling Fewer Vehicles At Better Prices?
items.summary: Headlines on Ford Motor (F) read like a business in retreat: a $1.3 billion net loss for the second quarter of 2026 and a 10.2% drop in U.S. sales in July. Underneath, second-quarter adjusted EBIT rose 17% to $2.5 billion as revenue fell 4% to $48.3 billion, and management lifted its 2026 adjusted EBIT guidance to a range of $10 billion to $11 billion.

items.title: Is Trending Stock General Motors Company (GM) a Buy Now?
items.summary: Recently, Zacks.com users have been paying close attention to General Motors (GM). This makes it worthwhile to examine what the stock has in store.

items.title: MP Trades at a Premium Valuation: Buy, Sell or Hold the Stock?
items.summary: MP's premium valuation faces scrutiny as losses, high costs and execution risks persist despite growth in rare earths and magnet production.

items.title: China’s Auto Threat Isn’t Just About EVs. Tesla Is Caught in the Middle.
items.summary: It’s about China and its plans to dominate the global auto market.  On Wednesday, Michigan Sen. Elissa Slotkin shot off a series of tweets on X, suggesting President Donald Trump might allow Chinese cars to be sold in America.  The White House didn’t respond to a request for comment.

items.title: Can Ford Overcome Tariff and Commodity Cost Headwinds in 2026?
items.summary: F raises its 2026 EBIT guidance despite tariff and commodity headwinds, while a Novelis aluminum recovery can drive a major second-half benefit.
